entities.summary:
The Austrian Football Association (Österreichischer Fußball-Bund, ÖFB), founded in 1904, serves as the governing body for association football in Austria and is headquartered in Vienna. It holds crucial significance in shaping the landscape of football not only in Austria but also in the broader context of European sports. The ÖFB was established at a time when football was rapidly gaining popularity across Europe, influenced by the establishment of football associations in neighboring countries such as Germany and England. Key figures in its formation included Hugo Meisl, who played an essential role in developing the national team and Austrian football culture during the early 20th century.

The ÖFB's early years saw the organization of regional leagues and the establishment of the Austrian Cup in 1919, which further promoted the sport across the nation. The association became a member of FIFA in 1904, contributing to the internationalization of football. Notably, the Austrian national team achieved significant success in the 1930s, including a remarkable performance at the 1934 FIFA World Cup, where they reached the semifinals. The ÖFB's administrative decisions and development programs have continued to influence the growth of football in Austria, leading to the establishment of a professional league system and youth development initiatives.
